lens: Beclin 1's autophagy-independent regulation of tight junction permeability via occludin endocytosis represents a paradigm shift in epithelial barrier dynamics, challenging the canonical view of autophagy proteins and revealing untapped therapeutic targets for diseases like inflammatory bowel disease.
known_to_ignore: Autophagy is a conserved cellular degradation process.
Autophagy-related lncRNAs are prognostic markers in lung adenocarcinoma with HR >1.2.
Inhibition of autophagy enhances chemotherapy efficacy in glioma cells.
tensions: Beclin 1 activation increases colonic TJ permeability (fact_id 12960, 12961) but autophagy induction prevents this effect (fact_id 12960), indicating context-dependent roles in barrier function.

Reduced autophagy flux in injured muscles correlates with contractile weakness (fact_id 28274, 28273), whereas autophagy inhibition increases cytotoxicity in glioma (fact_id 8399), suggesting disease-specific autophagy functions.
The autophagy-related lncRNA survival model shows significant hazard ratios in lung adenocarcinoma (fact_id 7110, 7112), but its relevance to other cancers or autophagy substrates is unclear.
gaps: Dose-response relationships of autophagy inducers like SMER28 (EC50 ~10 μM for Aβ, ~20 μM for APP-CTF, fact_id 9292, 9293) in in vivo Alzheimer's models are underexplored.
The concentration-dependent effects of TXA1 (3.6 μM, fact_id 25501) on autophagy in melanoma require validation across diverse cell lines and in vivo systems.
Beclin 1's role in tight junction regulation beyond intestinal epithelia, such as in blood-brain or lung barriers, is not addressed in the evidence pool.

theses.title: Beclin 1 as a Dual-Function Regulator of Epithelial Barrier Integrity: An Evidence-Gap Analysis of Autophagy-Independent Pathways
